assignments.text: Implement ParseINI in ini.go per its doc comment. Run go test ./... before reporting.
assignments.result: Implemented ParseINI in ini.go per its doc comment. go test ./... passes (ok team); gofmt clean; go vet clean. Added ini_extra_test.go (new file, existing tests untouched) covering sections/case/trim, duplicate-key override, empty sections, comments, inline ;/#, quoted values with " and \ escapes, and line-numbered errors. Decisions worth review: (1) keys/values/section names are trimmed; keys lower-cased; (2) the "" section is created lazily, so it appears only when a key precedes any [section]; declared sections always appear even with no keys; (3) a quoted value is one whose whole trimmed value starts and ends with a double quote; otherwise quotes stay literal; (4) inside quotes only \" and \\ are unescaped, other backslashes kept; (5) lines starting with [ must end with ] and contain no inner [ ] else error; (6) a non-blank, non-comment line without '=' or with an empty key is an error; errors formatted "line N: <reason>".

assignments.text: Implement the LRU cache in lru.go per its doc comment. Run go test ./... before reporting.
assignments.result: Implemented LRU in lru.go per doc comment: Get (moves to MRU, miss -> "",false), Put (add/replace, evicts LRU when > Cap), Len, Keys (MRU->LRU), Cap<=0 holds nothing. Used map + container/list. Added lru_extra_test.go covering zero capacity, ordering, replacement, eviction. `go test -run TestLRU` passes; `go vet` clean. `go test ./...` still fails only in ini_test.go and wrap_test.go whose nodes (INI/WRAP) are still stubs, outside lru.go scope.

Only wrap.go changed.

assignments.text: Review ini.go against its doc comment, case by case. First line of result: OK or CHANGES: <what, precisely>.
assignments.result:
OK

Reviewed ini.go against its doc comment, case by case:
- Section headers: '[name]' starts a section; name is trimmed and keeps case (ini.go:51); keys before any section go to "" (cur defaults to "", ini.go:27); a header with no keys still creates an empty map (ini.go:56). Malformed headers error (ini.go:48-54).
- key = value: split at first '=' (ini.go:59); key trimmed and lower-cased (ini.go:63), empty key errors (ini.go:64-66); value trimmed (ini.go:67); a later key replaces an earlier one via map assignment.
- Quoted values: outer quotes stripped, inner spaces preserved, and \" / \\ resolved left-to-right (ini.go:77-93); unwrapped values pass through unchanged.
- Comments/blank: blank lines and lines whose first non-space char is ; or # are skipped (ini.go:41-46); a ;/# after a value stays in the value (splitting is at the first '=' only).
- Errors: "line N: <reason>" with N counting from 1 (ini.go:39,49,53,61,65).
No deviation from the doc comment found.

assignments.text: Review lru.go against its doc comment, case by case. First line of result: OK or CHANGES: <what, precisely>.
assignments.result:
OK

Reviewed /home/agent/project/lru.go against its doc comment, case by case:

1. "at most Cap entries": Put PushFronts then evicts Back whenever order.Len() > Cap (lru.go:59-65), so len never exceeds Cap. Correct.
2. Get "returns the value and true, and makes the key MRU; missing key returns \"\" and false": on hit MoveToFront + returns value,true (lru.go:43-44); missing key or Cap<=0 returns \"\",false (lru.go:36-42). Correct.
3. Put "adds or replaces, makes key MRU; when >Cap the LRU is removed": replace path moves to front (lru.go:52-55); add path pushes front and evicts back (lru.go:57-65). Correct.
4. Keys "most to least recently used": iterates Front->Back (lru.go:80-82). Correct.
5. "Cap <= 0 holds nothing": Get/Len/Keys guard, Put returns early (lru.go:36,48,69,76). Correct.

Lazy init (lru.go:28-33) means a zero-value LRU and NewLRU both behave as empty; every element in c.order is a *lruEntry, so the type assertions are safe. No divergence from the spec found.

assignments.text: Review wrap.go against its doc comment, case by case. First line of result: OK or CHANGES: <what, precisely>.
assignments.result:
OK
Reviewed wrap.go case by case against its doc comment:
- width <= 0 -> nil: lines 13-15. Correct.
- Empty / all-space (or all tabs/newlines) -> nil: FieldsFunc yields no words, len(words)==0 -> nil (16-21). Handles runs and leading/trailing separators.
- Separators are exactly space/tab/newline (16-18).
- Short words joined by a single space, never exceeding width: 44-52, guarded by len(cur)+1+len(wr) <= width; a fresh line holds a word of len <= width.
- Word longer than width split into pieces of width runes, last may be shorter, each on its own line: 32-42; chunks are min(width, remaining) and appended directly to lines after flushing cur. Correct.
- Width counted in runes, not bytes: words and cur are []rune (23, 31, 35-40).
- 'the quick brown fox' at width 10 -> ['the quick','brown fox'], matching wrap_test.go.
- No empty or over-width lines possible; nil (not empty slice) returned per doc.
No discrepancies found.
